External / portable drive · Not detected / not showing up

External Hard Drive Not Showing Up or Detected

An external drive is a hard drive inside a case, plus a small bridge board that turns USB into the drive's own connection. The fault could be the cable, the port, the bridge board or the drive itself. Start with cheap, safe checks.

3/5 · Take care
Success odds: Varies

Cable and software checks are safe, but taking the drive out of its case can lock encrypted data or damage it.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • If your computer offers to Initialize or Format the drive, click Cancel. Either can erase your data.
  • Do not keep plugging and unplugging it if you hear clicking or the drive feels hot. That adds wear.
  • Do not open the drive's case yet. Many portable drives are encrypted or have USB soldered to the drive, so removing it can make data unreadable.

Your steps

0 of 7 done
  1. Show me how
    1. Use a different USB cable, ideally the one that came with the drive, and plug it directly into the computer, not into a hub.
    2. Try a different USB port, and for desktop-style drives check the power adapter is firmly plugged in at both ends.
  2. Show me how
    1. Plug the drive into another computer, ideally one with a different operating system.
    2. Works elsewhere: the problem is your computer, its drivers or its port. Fails everywhere: the drive or its bridge board is the likely cause.
  3. Show me how
    1. Windows: right-click the Start button, choose Disk Management. If a window pops up asking to initialize the disk, click Cancel. Mac: open Finder, Applications, Utilities, Disk Utility, then View, Show All Devices.
    2. Find your drive by its size. If it says Raw, Unallocated or Not Initialized, do not click Initialize, Format or Erase.
    3. Use TestDisk instead, ideally on an image (an exact copy of the whole drive saved as a file).

    Guide: How to use TestDisk to copy files off a driveGuide: How to make an image (exact copy) of a drive

  4. Show me how
    1. With the drive connected, rest a fingertip on it. A soft hum or vibration means it spins.
    2. Clicking, grinding or complete silence points to a drive fault. Unplug it and read our clicking or no-power guide.
  5. Show me how
    1. Windows: right-click the Start button, choose Device Manager, and look under Disk drives and Universal Serial Bus controllers. Mac: Apple menu, About This Mac (newer macOS: then More Info), System Report, USB.
    2. Listed as a USB device but with no disk: suspect the bridge board. Do not assume the drive inside is bad.
  6. Show me how
    1. Do not open the case or remove the drive unless you know the exact model has a normal SATA connector and no hardware encryption.
    2. Search the model number plus 'encryption' or 'SATA' to check, or ask a recovery professional.

    Guide: How to find a trustworthy data recovery professional

  7. Show me how
    1. Read SMART with CrystalDiskInfo (Windows), or on a Linux live USB with sudo smartctl -a /dev/sdX after sudo apt install smartmontools (some USB cases need sudo smartctl -d sat -a /dev/sdX). Some USB cases hide SMART, so a missing report does not mean it is fine.
    2. If errors show, follow our imaging guide with ddrescue. Always type the failing drive first and the empty destination second. If you swap them, the copy erases your data.
    3. Then run TestDisk or PhotoRec on the image file.

    Guide: How to check if a drive is healthy (SMART)Guide: How to make an image (exact copy) of a driveGuide: How to use TestDisk to copy files off a driveGuide: How to use PhotoRec to recover photos and files

Mission complete! 🎉 Check your recovered files open properly, then back them up in two places.

Tools you'll use

smartmontools

Free open-source suite that reads S.M.A.R.T. health data from drives to show early signs of failure.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

CrystalDiskInfo

Free Windows app that shows a drive's S.M.A.R.T. health status, temperature and other key attributes.

  • Windows
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

GNU ddrescue

Copies a failing drive to an image file, retrying bad areas so you work from a copy, not the original.

  • Linux · macOS
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

TestDisk

Free open-source tool that finds lost partitions and repairs boot sectors so files can be read again.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

PhotoRec

Free open-source file carver that recovers files by signature, even when the file system is damaged.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

🧑‍🔧 When to call a pro

If it is not detected on any computer with a good cable, or it is a soldered or encrypted portable with important data, stop and ask a professional.

How to find a trustworthy pro →

Questions people ask

Can I just take the drive out and plug it into my computer?

Sometimes, but not always. Some portables have no standard SATA port, and some encrypt data using the original case's board, so the data may look blank outside it.

How do I tell a bad enclosure from a bad drive?

If the drive spins and sounds normal but no disk appears on any computer, the bridge board may be bad. Clicking, grinding or silence points to the drive itself.

Should I format it when Windows asks?

No. Formatting can erase the data you want to save. Click Cancel and use TestDisk first.
